You have attempted this same task before and did not succeed. These are the plans you wrote after those attempts.
Trial #1: New plan: I prematurely declared "DONE" upon returning to the Utility room, failing to realize that the Attic still had an unvisited direction (east) that I had not explored in my second visit. My strategy of stopping immediately upon revisiting a room was flawed because it ignored the possibility of new paths emerging from previously visited nodes. Next time, I will maintain a mental map of visited rooms and, crucially, track which specific directions have been attempted from each room. I will only declare "DONE" when I am in a room where all available directions lead to rooms I have already visited *and* I have exhausted all untried directions from every room in my current path. Specifically, when I returned to the Attic the second time, I should have noticed I had not yet tried "east" from that location (having only tried "north" and "west" previously) and would have gone east instead of returning to the Utility room and stopping.
